sanskrit: māṃ vadantam anu sarve vadantu māṃ prāṇantam anu prāṇantu sarve | māṃ viśantam anu sarve viśantu mayi devā ekavṛto bhavantu ||
english: As I speak, let all speak after me; as I breathe, let all breathe after me; as I enter, let all enter after me — may the gods be united in me as one.

sanskrit: sūryo mā cakṣuṣaḥ pātu bṛhaspatir vācaḥ somo rājā sabhāyāḥ | indro vo dṛśe bhavāmi ||
english: May the Sun protect my sight, Bṛhaspati my speech, King Soma the assembly — I become Indra for your beholding.

sanskrit: veda vai te sabhe nāma subhadrāsi sarasvati | atho ye te sabhāsadas te me santu suvācasaḥ ||
english: I know your name, O Assembly — you are Subhadrā, O Sarasvatī; and those who sit in your assembly, may they speak well for me.

sanskrit: imā yā brahmaṇaspate viṣūcīr vāca īrate | sadhrīcīr indra tāḥ kṛtvā mahyaṃ śivatamāḥ kṛdhi ||
english: These scattered words that go in all directions, O Brahmaṇaspati — making them converge, O Indra, render them most auspicious for me.

sanskrit: aham eṣāṃ hastarasam ahaṃ vijñānam ā dade | sarvasyā asyāḥ saṃsado 'haṃ bhūyāsam uttama indro yo gāyatām iva ||
english: I seize the handshake-essence of these people and their discernment; may I be the foremost in this entire assembly, even as Indra is foremost among those who sing.

sanskrit: uttamaṃ mottame kṛdhy uttamā hi babhūvitha | yāṃ tvā bhuraṇyur anvaicchad gandharvaḥ śaradaḥ śatam ||
english: Make me the highest among the highest, for you yourself have become supreme — you whom the restless Gandharva sought for a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: abhibhūr aham āgamam ahaṃ bhūyāsam uttamaḥ | idaṃ pratipravādinaṃ dviṣantam ava dhūnve ||
english: I have come as one who overpowers; may I be the foremost. I shake down this adversary who speaks against me and harbors hatred.

sanskrit: uruṣ ṭe vastir bhavatu samudrasya bilaṃ yathā | parodakam iva sicyatāṃ mūtraṃ te tanvas pari ||
english: May your bladder become spacious like the cavity of the ocean; may your urine flow from your body as water pours from a distant source.

sanskrit: yathā vāto yathodakaṃ yathā samudra ejati | evā te garbha ejatu niraitu daśamāsyo bahir jarāyuṇā saha ||
english: As the wind stirs, as water stirs, as the ocean heaves — so may your womb stir; may the ten-month child come forth outward together with the placenta.

sanskrit: idam u śreyo 'vasānam āgāṃ śive me dyāvāpṛthivī abhūtām | asapatnāḥ pradiśo me bhavantu na vai tvā dviṣmo abhayaṃ no astu ||
english: I have come to this resting-place that is better; heaven and earth have become auspicious for me; may the directions be free of rivals for me — truly we bear no hatred toward you; may fearlessness be ours.

sanskrit: vāstoṣpata iha naḥ śarma yaccha bhadrāc chreyo abhi no neṣa vasyaḥ | ariṣṭā vīrā iha me bhavantu dvipāc catuṣpān mayy astu puṣṭam ||
english: O Lord of the Homestead, grant us shelter here; lead us from the auspicious to the better and more prosperous. May my heroes be unharmed here; may two-footed and four-footed beings thrive in me.

sanskrit: anamīvo vāstoṣpate viśvā rūpāṇy āviśan | sakhā suśeva edhi naḥ ||
english: O Lord of the Homestead, free from disease, entering into all forms — be a kind and gentle friend to us.

sanskrit: ṛtena sthūṇā adhi roha vaṃś- -ogro virājann apa vṛṅkṣva śatrūn | mā te riṣann upasattāro atra virājāṃ jīvāc charadaḥ śatāni ||
english: Ascend the post by the power of cosmic order, O mighty one shining resplendently, and cut away the enemies. May those who dwell near you not be harmed here; may he who shines brightly live a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: ā rohataṃ pakṣāv amṛtaṃ vasānau dampatyoḥ kṛṇutaṃ dīrgham āyuḥ | tatra nārī putriṇī jīvapatn- -īdaṃ kulāyam upasaṃviśāti ||
english: Rise up, you two wings clad in immortality; grant long life to the couple. There the woman with living sons and a living husband takes up her place in this nest.

sanskrit: agnir mā viśvād duritāt punātu mātariśvā pavamānaḥ purastāt somo mā pātu maruto bṛhaspatir vāyuś ca mā pavamānaḥ punītām ||
english: May Agni purify me from all evil; may Mātariśvan, the purifying wind, do so from the east; may Soma protect me; may the Maruts, Bṛhaspati, and Vāyu the purifying wind purify me.

sanskrit: tvayā satyaṃ vi jayante tava satyaṃ vivācanam | agre vṛkṣasya jāyase semaṃ janaya pūruṣam ||
english: By you, truth is won in debate; your truth is the decisive utterance. You are born at the tip of the tree — give birth to this man.

sanskrit: vṛkṣasya śataśākhasya mādhuntasya nikṛtvanaḥ | vibhīdakasya yat phalaṃ tena tvon mādayāmasi ||
english: With the fruit of the vibhīdaka tree — that tree of a hundred branches, the honey-sweet one, the one that strips away — with that we intoxicate you.

sanskrit: pūrve vātāt pra patataṃ pūrve patatam aśvibhyām | ime nyarvaṇī aham udnevāgnim avīvare ||
english: Fly forth before the wind; fly forth before the Aśvins. These two swift ones — I have kindled the fire as one pours a libation upward.

sanskrit: mā yakṣmam iha hāsiṣṭa mā riphanto vi gātana | subhūtam asmabhyaṃ dhatta yuṣmān anv etu kilbiṣam ||
english: Do not leave disease behind here; do not go away muttering. Bestow well-being upon us; let sin follow after you.

sanskrit: iha varca iha paya iha cakṣur upa hvaye | ihendriyaṃ dadhātana ||
english: Here I summon vigor, here milk, here eyesight. Establish virile power here.

sanskrit: ā hi harī apaptatām imaṃ vatsaṃ vanād iyam | apakāmaṃ hy aghnye vatso devi mamāra te ||
english: The two tawny ones have flown hither; this cow has come from the forest to this calf. Against your will, O inviolable cow, O goddess, your calf has died.

sanskrit: ye tvopavidur vidur nijavatseva dohasva | ahaṃ te veda saṃmanaḥ saṃvananasya veda te ||
english: Those who have come to know you — they know. Yield milk as for your own calf. I know your concord; I know the means of winning you over.

sanskrit: eṣa te aghnye vatsas taṃ vāñcha | tāṃ satyoktiṃ brūmaḥ ||
english: This is your calf, O inviolable cow — long for him. This true word we speak.

sanskrit: yā sarasvatī govananī sā vāmenāṅkasā nyetya | imāṃ gāṃ vānayatu svāhā ||
english: She who is Sarasvatī, the one who wins cattle — let her come near with her auspicious flank and make this cow yield. Svāhā!
